properties.content:
Report Details

Comments: On location to witness the conclusion of 72 hr. Stepped Pressure Build Up Tests (SPBUTs) being performed on all (5) wells on the Hunter pad., the Hunter 21HC, 22HC, 23HC, 5H and 6H. These SPBUTs are being performed to assess the recent remedial work, CET (Casing Expansion Tool), deployment performed on all (5) Hunter wells production casing strings. This is the 5th post CET deployment PBUTs being performed on these wells. - All (5) wells on the pad are in production. The (20x13) annuli are capped and set up to vent to atmosphere via Sentry valves. The (13x9) and the (9x5) annuli are set up to vent to a production tank via 2" common vent line. All annuli were closed when I arrived. - Upon arrival I met with CALLC Field Rep. Tyler Sites and Dalton Johnson and Creston Consultant Reps., Tom Messing and Andrew Pfisterer. Starting at approx. 10:45 ending annuli pressures were checked using a digital Crystal gauge. Gas checks were performed by Creston Reps., using a Bascom Turner Gas Explorer meter. Creston Consultants collected gas samples off annuli, where present, and will send out for isotopic analysis. - Ending pressures, gas checks and time of gas sample collections are listed below for all the HUNTER Pad wells. - HUNTER 5H: (20x13): 0.0 psi.; 1,820 ppm peak dropping off to 0% CH4; No sample collected (13x9): 10 psi.; 77% CH4; Sample collected @ 10:50 (9x5): 275 psi.; 89% CH4; Sample collected at 10:55 - HUNTER 6H: (20x13): 0.0 psi.; 0% CH4; No sample collected (13x9): 0.0psi.; 68% CH4; Sample collected @ 11:10 (9x5): 405 psi.; 88% CH4; Sample collected @ 11:15 - HUNTER 22HC: (20x13): 2.0 psi.; 75 % CH4; Sample collected @ 11:20 (13x9): 2.0 psi.; 79% CH4; Sample collected @ 11:25 (9x5): 146 psi.; 86% CH4; Sample collected @ 11:30 - HUNTER 21HC: (20x13): 0.0 psi.; 3,500 ppm dropping off to 0% CH4; No sample collected (13x9): 3 psi.; 79% CH4; Sample collected @ 11:35 (9x5): 69 psi.; 78% CH4; Sample collected @ 11:40 - HUNTER 23HC: (20x13): 0.0 psi.; 160 ppm dropping off to 0% CH4; No sample collected (13x9): 2 psi.; 77% CH4; Sample collected @ 11:45 (9x5): 70 psi.; 79% CH4; Sample collected @ 11:50 - All (5) wells (20x13) annuli were returned to open and venting to atmosphere via Sentry valves and the (13x9) and (9x5) annuli were opened and venting to production tank @ 12:00.

Unconventional: Yes

Inspection Type: Incident- Response to Accident or Event

Comments: Incident inspection of Repsol's "Morgan 073" Marcellus well site.Harry Lammy (Repsol) called the DEP on Wednesday October 30, 2024 to report an estimated 20 gallon produced liquid release to the south end of the pad surface that day.Murray Kush (Repsol, Company Man) showed me where the produced liquid spill occurred when a vac truck overfilled on the south end of the pad surface near the gray cylindrical tanks. Gas Field Services removed the impacted pad material with guidance from Resource Management and placed it in an open top dumpster within 24 hours of the release. Soil in the remediated area has electrical conductivity of 0.02 mS/cm with a Hanna Soil Test meter. I did not observe any residual impacts from the spill. Violations for the spill are considered immediately corrected.Repsol expanded the flat pad area at this site February - May 2023. They spudded 4 new conductors on March 27, 2023. Precision Drilling 572 drilled the new wells into the Marcellus Shale in February-April 2024, adding to the existing 4 Marcellus wells at this site. Pro Frac hydraulically fractured the 4 new Marcellus wells here August 29-September 16, 2024. Repsol started flowing back liquid from the 4 new Marcellus wells on October 12, 2024 into the 37 tanks on the south end of the pad. They expect to finish flowback operations in about 1 week. Vegetation, rock, and erosion blanket stabilize soil of the site. I did not see accelerated erosion or sedimentation.Post Construction Stormwater Management (PCSM) controls are in place and appear to be functioning as designed. Repsol constructed a new bioretention basin on the south end of the site, and removed the old basin.Containment structures are intact. I did not observe any leaks or other deficiencies.I did not see any pooled water on the pad surface. Moist soil in 3 separate areas on the pad has electrical conductivity of 0.02-0.12 mS/cm with a Hanna Soil Test.Air temp 63FJLP

Comments: Inspection Report 1 of 2On 03/03/2026, a routine partial inspection was conducted at the John Hunter Well Site in Donegal Township, Washington County (37-125-28285). I was accompanied by Water Quality Specialist Sara Trio (PA DEP).The following was observed:-Act 9 sign (Photo 1).-Sediment-laden water flowing from access road and site to culvert inlet (Photos 2-4). Recommend access road maintenance.-Culvert inlet pipe receiving road fines and sediment-laden water (Photos 5,6).-Culvert outlet area appears to be pooling/discharging sediment; visible from access road (Photos 7,8). Recommend maintenance and adequately functioning environmental controls design and application in all drainage areas.-Accelerated erosion flow path downslope from culvert outlet (Photos 9-11).-Existing Compost Filter Sock (CFS) appears overtaken by wood debris and vegetation; sediment deposition from what appears to be significant flow downslope (Photos 12,13). Recommend maintenance and adequately functioning environmental controls design and application in all drainage areas.-Flow path of sediment-laden water continued downslope (Photos 14-16).-Sediment deposit concentrated area (Photos 17,18).-Flow path of sediment-laden water discharging into unnamed tributary flowing to Little Wheeling Creek (Photos 19,20).-Further down access road toward pad, culvert inlet and outlet related to inspection report 2 of 2 appears receiving and discharging sediment-laden water; accelerated erosion and sediment flow path downslope into wooded area offsite (Photos 21,22).Range Resources Environmental Compliance Specialist Dennis Furmanek was contacted on 03/04/2026 regarding observations noted above.Recommendations as noted above.Due to the discharge of sediment from the site capable of reaching waters of the Commonwealth and failure to minimize accelerated erosion and sedimentation, violations of 102.4(b)1, 102.11(a), 78a.53, 102.4(b)4, 102.11(A)2, CSL 301, and CSL 307(a) are being issued.

Comments: On February 5 2024, the Department conducted a follow up inspection of the Cole 1 OG Well in response to IR 3641696.The findings are as follows:The site appears to be unchanged from the Department's previous inspection on 12/12/23. The previously observed fine, light colored material, identified by operator representive Joel Greco as fine limestone material was observed again. The fine limestone material still appeared to be holding an excess amount of water resulting in the ground surrounding the production tank to be soft and not properly stabilized. On 12/13/2023 the Department spoke to Mr.Greco on the phone regarding the previously observed stabilization concerns with the material and Mr.Greco stated that the material would stabilize after it dries once, allowing it to compact. However, at the time of this inspection the fine limestone material has not stabilized and is still soft, resulting in improper stabilization which increases the potential for accelerated erosion and sedimentation to occur. Based on today's inspection, violations associated with the spill remain open as it does not appear the operator has complied with the Department's Spill Policy at this time. Additional violations are being issued for improper site stabilization.

The DEP traveled the area of the impact beginning at the release point (CTS #396090) (photo #2). The stormwater basin with containment has one 24/7 water truck recovering fluids on top of and underneath the containment and from the sumps. On 04/03/2026 an additional sump was installed further down gradient (photo #9). The additional sump is manned 24/7. Fluids are recovered from the sump ~ every hour. The EC of the fluids entering UNT to Rockwell Creek upstream of the confluence were ~ 935 us/cm (photo #14). Fluids on the pad surface were field measured for EC between 430-640 us/cm. There was no evidence of any additional spills or releases. Proper secondary containment was observed throughout the site. Stimulation activities are to be continued until 04/30/2026.Violations remain open against API #015-23994. We departed at 1115 hours.

properties.summary: Environmental Health & Safety violation issued on 6/08/2026 to TRINITY MINERAL PARTNERS LLC in Sugar Grove Township, Warren county. CSL 402(b) - POTENTIAL POLLUTION - Conducting an activity regulated by a permit issued pursuant to Section 402 of The Clean Streams Law to prevent the potential of pollution to waters of the Commonwealth without a permit or contrary to a permit issued under that authority by the Department.
properties.content:
Report Details
Inspection Client: TRINITY MINERAL PARTNERS LLC
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 6/08/2026
Violation Code: CSL 402(b) - POTENTIAL POLLUTION - Conducting an activity regulated by a permit issued pursuant to Section 402 of The Clean Streams Law to prevent the potential of pollution to waters of the Commonwealth without a permit or contrary to a permit issued under that authority by the Department.
Violation ID: 8277566
Permit API: 123-47222
Unconventional: No
County: Warren
Municipality: Sugar Grove Township
Inspection Type: Routine/Complete Inspection
Inspection Date: 6/08/2026
Comments: A discharge of production fluids is evident at the Loomis Lease tank battery. Elevated specific conductance in soils was observed beneath one of the stock tank's drain valves within the secondary containment area as well as throughout a swath of stressed and dead vegetation downslope of the Loomis Lease tank battery. Brian Ayers (WQSS-DEP) and I (Mat Haemer WQS-DEP) were present for this inspection.Evidence of a concentrated flow of fluids was observed just beyond the secondary containment diking. Bare soils outside of containment were observed to have been eroded in a manner consistent with the channelized flow of a large volume of fluid. The bottom of the eroded channel was found to have elevated specific conductance in excess of 2,000 micro Siemens per centimeter.Areas downslope of the tank battery where the flow of fluid was observed to widen (visible via the wide swath of stressed and dead vegetation) were observed to have elevated specific conductance in soils in excess of 5,000 micro Siemens per centimeter.The downslope path of the released fluid was then captured by a lease road ditch approximately 150 feet downslope of the tank battery. Observations of elevated specific conductance in soils within the road ditch continued to a culvert nearby to the Loomis Lease Loomis 3 OG well. Standing water at the outflow of this culvert was found to have elevated specific conductance in excess of 1,300 micro Siemens per centimeter. Elevated soil conductivity readings in excess of 1,000 micro Siemens per centimeter continued for approximately 100 feet from the outfall of the culvert.The total observed path of stressed/dead vegetation and elevated conductivity readings was approximately 750 feet in length and up to 30 feet in width. Because the volume of this release exceeds the 1 bbl threshold, the use of either the Act 2 or Alternative Remediation Process is required.It is requested that Trinity Mineral Partners provide the Department with receipts documenting the proper disposal of brine resulting from producing the Loomis Lease.

Comments: On 12/18/2025, an incident inspection was conducted at the John Briggs Well pad in Aleppo Township, Greene County for a reported release (CTS: 394097). I was accompanied by DEP Water Quality Specialist Sara Trio.The spill was reported to the Department by the operator on 12/11/2025 through the DEP Emergency Hotline. It was reported that the piping inside the 50U Gas Processing Unit (GPU) washed out and produced fluids spilled off containment and onto the well pad. The amount reported was greater than 5 gallons and the spill was contained to the well pad. Specialized Professional Services, Inc (SPSI) was on site the same day to begin clean up.The following was observed during the inspection:- The spill area was observed adjacent to the 50U GPU. The impacted gravel was excavated. Absorbent material was observed behind the GPU (Photos 1-3).- Conductivity readings were taken throughout the spill area. Elevated conductivity was observed in two small holes sumps that collected fluids (Photos 4-6). Elevated conductivity was also observed behind the GPU near the absorbent material (Photo 7).- Additional conductivity readings were taken throughout and outside of the spill area. They were all observed to be below clean up standards (Photos 8-12).It appears the spill still needs additional remediation in certain areas. The Department requests information on the amount spilled and how the amount was verified.Violations of 78a.54, SWMA 301, 78a57(a), and 91.34(a) are being issued for the spill.

Comments: Incident Inspection of Expand's "Oil Can" Marcellus well site.Steve Moyer (Expand) called the DEP on Monday (Preisdents Day) February 16, 2026 to report an estimated 30 gallon release of produced liquid (brine) from a tank battery. Moyer explained that a vac truck was filling a 500 barrel tank with brine and it overflowed into secondary liner containment. Approximately 3 gallons of the brine splashed onto the pad surface, and a liner breach leaked some of the brine onto the pad surface. The brine is stored on this pad for hydraulically fracturing Marcellus wells at other Expand sites. Expand removed 4 of the 500 barrel tanks February 18-19 to expose the impacted pad surface for excavation.I spoke with Dakota Manning (Crescent Environmental) on site. He explained they are removing liquid from snow melt that is flowing into the excavated area. They plan to obtain soil samples to comply with Act 2 after the melt liquid stops flowing into the sump. Crescent got electrical conductivity readings of 0.6-1.0 mS/cm from the liquid in the sump.Violations for the brine release are cited to the 015-21874 permit.Cannot assess soil stabilization because ~6 of snow cover. I did not see accelerated erosion or sedimentation.Containment structures are intact. I did not observe any leaks or other deficiencies.There is snow in all 3 Marcellus cellars.Post Construction Stormwater Management (PCSM) controls are in place and appear to be functioning as designed.Pooled liquid on the pad surface has electrical conductivity of 0.15-0.33 mS/cm with an Oakton PCTS5.Air temp 24FJLP

Comments: On 02/08/2024, a restoration inspection was conducted at the Ironman 2H well following the receipt of a Post Drilling Well Site Restoration Report. The access road was in generally good condition (Photo 1).The wellhead was in generally good condition and equipped with a well tag displaying the operator and wells information (Photos 2, 3).There was no drilling equipment on site (Photos 4-8).The GPU was in generally good condition and on containment (Photo 9). The other tank has been removed from the site (Photo 15).The date of the final well drilled or expired was 11/20/2014. The Post Drilling Well Site Restoration Report was submitted in 2024. A violation of 78a65(e) is being issued and immediately corrected. I recommend that the Post Drilling Well Site Restoration Report be approved.

Unconventional: No

Comments: Cement plugs were set in well bore on 04/21/2021. An inspection was conducted on 04/21, as well as on 04/28/2021, when the top hole section of well bore was being filled with pea gravel. Fluid in wellbore was static during both inspections. A vent monument had been set in the top of the surface casing, but had not yet been cemented in place. During todays inspection, a significant amount of bubbling was observed in the fluid inside of the surface casing. An Altair 5x gas meter was used to check the vent and the bubbling fluid for stray has. Methane reading was 27% volume in the vent, and 10% volume at the top of fluid. Gas is likely entering the well bore in the 1500'-1150' range. Pea gravel and casing seat plug will have to be drilled out in order to assess necessary remedial procedures. I will inspect the well one week from today to determine if the venting gas is residual. Violations cannot be closed until the vertical flow of gas to surface has been eliminated. Tatonka Oil Co. representative Tom Lenhortt has been made aware of my findings.

Report Details
Inspection Client: CHESAPEAKE APPALACHIA LLC
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 12/28/2022
Violation Code: 78.56(a) - PITS AND TANKS FOR TEMPORARY CONTAINMENT - Operator failed to contain pollutional substances and wastes from the drilling, altering, completing, recompleting, servicing and plugging the well, including brines, drill cuttings, drilling muds, oils, stimulation fluids, well treatment and servicing fluids, plugging and drilling fluids other than gases in a pit, tank or series of pits and tanks.
Violation ID: 987254
Permit API: 015-22203
Unconventional: Yes
County: Bradford
Municipality: Tuscarora Twp
Inspection Type: Administrative/File Review
Inspection Date: 3/07/2023
Comments: On 3/7/2023, DEP representatives John Rogers conducted an Administrative inspection on the Chesapeake Maggie well site. This inspection is to report the results of a water sample that was collected from a water puddle on the west corner of the Maggie well site.During an inspection on 12/28/2022, the department discovered high conductance fluid on the well pad surface outside of containment. The fluid covered a 50' x 50' area and was field tested in different areas with results being >20.0 mS. 20.0 mS is the upper limit of the Oakton PCTS-50 meter. The department collected a sample of the water for laboratory analysis from location N 41.684052 W -76.121972.On 2/22/2023 the department received the results of the laboratory analysis that shows elevated aluminum, barium, iron, magnesium, sodium, strontium, and chlorides and is indicative of regulated substances being released onto the pad. The sample report is displayed in pictures 1 and 2. Chesapeake is pursuing Act 2 for the site in response to that incident.The release of fluid with elevated conductance to the pad surface constitutes violations of SWMA 301, CSL 402, 25 PA Code78a.56(a) and 78.66(b)(2).Violations are still outstanding for inspection ID 3482654 for high conductance fluid being discovered on the pad surface.
